title: The Trail of Mount Kessler
premise: Jude Joubert, a salvage diver who left the mountains fifteen years ago after a betrayal she refuses to name, is hired by her old rival Cass Merrow to recover a sealed strongbox from the wreck of the Kessler Star — a job the crew's late captain swore off and the navy quietly patrols. The box holds proof that the town of Kessler's founding fortune was stolen from Jude's own family, and Cass wants it not for justice but for leverage over the mining dynasty that now runs the valley. As the crew crosses the range ahead of the early snows, pursued by the dynasty's fixer and shadowed by the truth of what Jude did to earn her exile, she must decide whether power reclaimed through blackmail simply changes hands rather than ends. In the end, Jude burns the proof on the summit, choosing belonging with her crew over vengeance, and descends into winter as someone finally at home in her own name.
about_author: Vesper Sterling is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who writes adventure stories set in the cold places where people go to lose themselves. Sterling lives off-grid half the year and claims every book begins with a map and a grudge.

chapters.title: Fathoms and Miles
chapters.summary: Jude Joubert dives a navy-restricted wreck off the coast, measuring her life in miles traveled rather than years lived. POV: Jude. Establishes her restless competence and deliberate rootlessness; the emotional beat is the comfort of never staying anywhere long enough to be known.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: Cass Merrow arrives at the dock with a contract: salvage the Kessler Star, the one job their dead captain forbade. POV: Jude. Old resentment flares alongside curiosity; Jude signs not for money but because Cass says the box has her family's name inside it.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Jude meets the hired crew — engineer Okafor, young climber Tamsin, and quiet navigator Reyes — each carrying reasons to need this crossing. POV: Jude. She tests them the way she tests rope, looking for flaws; the beat is reluctant respect forming despite herself.

chapters.title: What the Captain Swore
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: fifteen years ago, Captain Ilsa Voss refused the Kessler job and made everyone swear it off, the night Jude's brother disappeared into the range. POV: Jude. Guilt surfaces; Jude realizes she may have caused the very exile she's been running from.

chapters.title: The Navy Won't Discuss It
chapters.summary: A patrol boat shadows them out of harbor; an officer warns them off with words too rehearsed to be routine. POV: Reyes. The navigator reads the pursuit as professional interest, not law; the beat is the crew realizing they're being hunted before they've even started.

chapters.title: Into the Range
chapters.summary: The crew leaves the coast and enters the mountain approach as weather windows begin closing early this year. POV: Tamsin. The young climber idolizes Jude and sees her fear of the mountains for the first time; the beat is awe curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Kessler Town
chapters.summary: Resupply in the company town reveals the Aldous mining dynasty's grip — company scrip, company church, company sheriff. POV: Jude. She walks streets her family once owned; the emotional beat is grief sharpening into resolve as she sees what was taken.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Dynasty fixer Edran Pike offers to buy the crew out over dinner, politely naming each of their debts and secrets. POV: Cass. Her POV reveals she's hiding her own history with the Aldouses; the beat is Cass lying smoothly while realizing Pike knows more than he should.

chapters.title: The Wreck Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: They reach the Kessler Star, wrecked decades ago high on a glacier shelf, impossibly far from any water. POV: Jude. Diving a frozen hull, she finds the strongbox compartment empty except for a map scratched by her brother's hand; the beat is vertigo and hope.

chapters.title: Brother's Hand
chapters.summary: Deciphering the scratched map, Jude learns her brother reached the wreck alive and hid the box deeper in the range. POV: Jude interleaved with Tamsin. Grief becomes purpose; the beat is Jude admitting aloud, for the first time, that her brother didn't just vanish — he was running from her.

chapters.title: Pike's People
chapters.summary: Dynasty men hit the camp at night; Reyes is injured covering the retreat and the crew loses half their supplies. POV: Reyes. His stoic navigation of pain mirrors his navigation of the group; the beat is the crew hardening from hires into something like family.

chapters.title: Cass's Confession
chapters.summary: Trapped in a storm shelter, Cass admits the Aldouses ruined her family too, and that leverage — not justice — has kept her alive for years. POV: Cass. The rivals' old wound opens honestly; the beat is fragile alliance replacing competition.

chapters.title: The High Col
chapters.summary: The crew attempts the pass ahead of schedule as the snows arrive early; a crevasse fall nearly takes Tamsin, saved by Jude's rigging. POV: Tamsin. Hero worship matures into seeing Jude as flawed and human; the beat is trust earned through failure, not success.

chapters.title: The Hidden Cache
chapters.summary: Following the scratched map to an ice cave, they find the strongbox — and her brother's journal, recording how the Aldouses' founder murdered for the fortune and how Ilsa Voss helped cover it up. POV: Jude. The revelation shatters her loyalty to the dead captain; the beat is betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: What Jude Did
chapters.summary: The journal also records the night of the disappearance: Jude, then seventeen, told the Aldouses where her brother would be, believing she was protecting him from Ilsa's plan. POV: Jude. Full confession to the crew; the beat is the terror of being truly known — and not being abandoned.

chapters.title: Pike Closes In
chapters.summary: Pike's men take the pass behind them; a radio call offers amnesty for the box and names Cass as the one who sold the route to the dynasty months ago. POV: Cass. Her past double-dealing detonates the alliance; the beat is Jude facing a second betrayal by someone she'd begun to trust.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: The crew fractures: Okafor argues for the deal, Tamsin for the truth, Reyes for survival. Cass disappears in the night with the box. POV: Okafor. His pragmatism gets its fullest hearing; the beat is the painful recognition that power corrupts even the righteous plans to seize it.

chapters.title: The Summit Chase
chapters.summary: Jude climbs alone through the storm to the peak where Cass waits, box open, transmission beacon lit for Pike. POV: alternating Jude/Cass. Confrontation at altitude; the beat is two women recognizing themselves in each other's hunger for what was stolen.

chapters.title: Burn the Proof
chapters.summary: Above the clouds, Jude chooses: she burns the documents rather than let Cass or the Aldouses wield them, keeping only her brother's journal. POV: Jude. Climax of the theme — power destroyed instead of transferred; the beat is liberation and loss in the same breath.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Pike's men arrive to ash and a blizzard; Cass, choosing Jude at last, helps turn them back before the crew reunites for the descent. POV: Cass. Redemption without absolution; the beat is Cass accepting consequences she can't negotiate away.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unwanted
chapters.summary: In Kessler Town, the crew exposes enough of the truth publicly to crack the dynasty's hold, though no fortune changes hands. POV: Tamsin. Justice as erosion, not explosion; the beat is satisfaction tempered by the cost, and the town beginning to breathe.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Spring: Jude stays at the coast one full season, diving the same waters, fixing her own mooring line. POV: Jude. She measures time in years now, not miles; the final beat is belonging chosen daily — with the crew, with her brother's memory, with her own name.
